Lauren — putting technical assumptions here so we have a single record. Below I filled the worksheet with per-workload guidance. Key points / assumptions: 

1) Workload mapping / GPU SKUs- Conversational LLMs (8k context): H100 80GB (float16 mixed) for peak-latency sensitive workloads; A100 80GB for steady baseline if cost prioritized.
- Conversational LLMs (32k context or extended): H100 preferred due to memory footprint; consider multi-node packing for high concurrency.
- Embeddings & Reranking: L4 / T4-class for embeddings at high QPS; A10/A30 equivalents for mid-tier reranking pipelines.

2) Throughput and tail latency (typical per-model baseline)
- H100 (8k): baseline single-GPU throughput ~ 180 tokens/sec for large chat models; P95 ~ 110ms, P99 ~ 320ms at target 80% utilization.
- A100 (8k): baseline ~ 140 tokens/sec; P95 ~ 160ms, P99 ~ 420ms at 75% utilization.
- L4 (embeddings): embeddings throughput ~ 1200 reqs/sec (small batch) with P95 < 60ms.

Notes: numbers assume Redwood runtime optimizations (continuous batching, KV cache for chat, quantized kernels where applicable). We should provide both tokens/sec and RPS for Orbit's model mix. I added per-SKU sheets with packing guidance and concurrency lanes in the spreadsheet.

3) Burst strategy
- Recommend two lanes: reserved pool (committed capacity) and burst lane (ephemeral queue with higher cost). Fallbacks: route to quantized model variant or lower-context variant if tail latency exceeds SLOs.

Attached: updated draft_commitment_matrix.xlsx (sheet: technical_assumptions).

--
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Quick commercial take to pair with Karthik's tech assumptions:

1) Commitment tiers (examples)
- Tier A (Standard Reserved): 6-month commitment, billed monthly, 10% discount vs on-demand, recommended for baseline throughput.
- Tier B (Reserved + Burst): 12-month commitment with burst lane credits (X% of baseline hours) and 18% discount.
- Tier C (Enterprise): Multi-year, dedicated pool with custom SLAs (99.95%), priority scheduling, and custom eviction policies.

2) Minimums / slotting
- Minimum reserved pool suggested: equivalent of 4 H100 GPUs for initial pilot (to guarantee predictability). Slotting for fleet: add 10-20% headroom for maintenance and regional failover.

3) Pricing & TCO considerations
- Provide per-GPU hourly and monthly committed price in the worksheet. Include conversion to $/1M tokens for their conversational mix.

4) SLA and fallback language
- Offer P95/P99 targets per SKU at committed utilization. Include automatic fallback: when reserved saturated, traffic can either use burst lane (higher rate) or be routed to compatible model variants (quantized) with explicit impact notes.

I'll populate the commercial sheet in draft_commitment_matrix.xlsx and add a short pricing band. Monica — please validate onboarding lead times (we usually need ~6 weeks to provision & validate in Dedicated for a new account).

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Dedicated Sales, Redwood Inference
